A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same work, renamed from Free3D to LaxMotion, with matching authors, core equations, datasets, and retained results. Both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplementary files; supplementary material mentioned in the text is not included.

before.justification: V1 reports original HumanML3D and KIT-ML evaluations, component ablations, reconstruction experiments, and qualitative motion-generation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and qualitative results and adds global/relative-motion comparisons and experiments varying input and supervision granularity.

M1.justification: The trajectory/limb factorization and projection, cross-view reconstruction, orientation, and feature-consistency losses match across versions. MDM-based and 3D-finetuned variants already appear in v1. V2's generic generator formulation and explicit 3D-trajectory description clarify and reframe the procedure without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: HumanML3D, KIT-ML, and the microgravity and underwater examples remain. V2 adds a trajectory-free relative-motion evaluation setting on HumanML3D in Table 3, extending task conditions without adding a dataset or domain.

E2.justification: V2 adds a directly relevant comparison against 2D-based generation approaches: MAS under global motion and Motion-2-to-3 under global and relative motion in Table 3. MoMask also participates in the relative-motion comparison. The fully supervised comparator sets in Tables 1–2 are retained, but the new comparison substantially broadens the evidence beyond that category.

E3.justification: QM changes from sqrt(MModality/FID) in v1 Equation 16 to MModality/sqrt(FID) in v2 Equation 12, changing its weighting of diversity. V2 also introduces global/relative evaluation and full-versus-relaxed input/supervision controls, evaluated after feature fusion and fine-tuning in Table 4. These are metric and evaluation-design changes, not evidence that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 Table 4 adds a central ablation separating relaxed inputs from relaxed supervision through Full/Relax, Relax/Full, and Relax/Relax configurations. Conversely, v1's encoder-sharing ablation and its discussion disappear. The regularization, VAE-versus-AE, and limb-vector representation studies remain as v2 Tables 5–7.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals in Tables 1–2 and point estimates for ablations. Neither specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, or formal significance tests. Changed interval values accompany revised results rather than a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Reported 3D-finetuned HumanML3D FID changes from 0.038 to 0.034 and MultiModality from 2.090 to 2.529; KIT-ML FID changes from 0.153 to 0.135. HumanML3D MDM-based results also change, while retained MoMask-based raw scores match. V2 adds Tables 3–4 results, removes the no-sharing row, and omits MMDist from Tables 1–2. Increased QM values use a different definition and are not same-metric gains.

T1.justification: The QM formula is substantively redefined from sqrt(MModality/FID) to MModality/sqrt(FID), a non-equivalent mathematical definition. The principal motion-factorization and regularization equations otherwise retain their substance; neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: V1 claims training without any 3D motion annotations and entirely from 2D data. V2 narrows this to no direct 3D pose supervision while explicitly using 3D trajectories and mocap-derived projections. Contributions shift from a specifically named lifting architecture to a broader supervision-granularity framework, materially revising the central claim's scope.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies that its findings do not mean 3D data are unnecessary and interprets the new global/relative and relaxation comparisons as evidence for structural representations. The encoder-sharing explanation is removed. The underlying interpretation that relaxed supervision discourages coordinate memorization and supports diversity remains.

D1.justification: V1 specifies RVQ depth, codebook sizes, convolutional depth, Adam, batch size, learning rates, training stages, and MoMask inference steps. V2 replaces much of this with baseline references. It newly documents projected-mocap supervision and the diffusion prior treatment, but substantially reduces self-contained implementation information; referenced fusion details are not present in the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: V2 adds MAS, MVLift, and Motion-2-to-3 and substantially revises the weakly supervised discussion around existing motion-generation approaches. Novelty is repositioned around supervision granularity versus coordinate objectives and 3D fine-tuning. The CLIP reference disappears with the MoMask preliminary section.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming Free3D to LaxMotion, v2 extensively rewrites the introduction, method narrative, contributions, and conclusion around relaxed supervision. It removes the standalone MoMask preliminary section and reorganizes the method into representation reformulation, relaxed observability, and regularization.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column format. Figure 2 is redesigned from a full generation pipeline into a regularization diagram; Figure 3 rearranges the examples and shows additional frames. Two tables are added, main comparison tables lose MMDist columns, and retained ablation tables gain QM columns.

improvement.justification: V2 improves credibility by aligning its central claim with the use of 3D trajectories and adding relevant 2D-based comparisons and supervision controls. These gains are offset by reduced implementation detail and a new numerical inconsistency: Section 4.2 still gives fine-tuned HumanML3D FID as 0.038, whereas Table 1 reports 0.034. The net improvement is limited rather than substantial.
